backtest_protocol.execution_model: SEC event metadata uses PIT-safe usable_trade_date. Event-family burst membership is computed only from rows sharing the same usable_trade_date and event_family_bucket. OHLCV filters are observed through the signal-date close; paper entry is the next available open with production entry slippage; exit is ten trading days after the signal with target-side sell slippage and ROUND_TRIP_COST_PCT.

gate2.note: The sleeve uses only same-day and trailing OHLCV fields plus next-open/exit prices available to the replay. It does not ask LLM or production to infer hidden fields.
runtime_fields: SPY OHLCV rows for same-window relative strength

gate3.note: No core filter or live entry rule was added. The target source is additive default-off paper, so core survival is unchanged.

gate_questions.1_alpha_hypothesis: candidate_pool / entry: a same-event-family SEC burst of exactly two tickers may represent focused sector/theme attention rather than broad crowded filing days.

2_history_check.exp-20260529-010_and_011: SEC Item 2.02 peer-transfer variants were rejected. This run does not buy peers; it only evaluates the filing issuer itself when the event-family burst is exactly two.
2_history_check.exp-20260530-006: Read-only event-family burst attribution rejected the broad high-burst field, but its small_burst_2 bucket was positive in all three windows. This run tests that separate field as a formal paper candidate source.
2_history_check.exp-20260530-012: SEC sector-event breadth candidate pool was rejected. This run uses ticker-level event-family burst membership, not sector breadth or peer transfer.

gate_questions.4_acceptance_standard: Same three docs/backtesting.md windows; positive aggregate EV/PnL; no EV- or PnL-regressed window; >=20 paper trades across all 3 windows; drawdown drift <=0.5pp; survival >=5%; concentration inside guardrails.

hypothesis: SEC filings that occur in exactly two-ticker same-day same-event-family bursts may capture focused event attention without crowded high-burst reversal; with PIT SEC metadata and OHLCV confirmation they may provide a free-data default-off candidate-pool source.
interpretation: The SEC small event-family burst candidate pool did not clear Gate 4. Do not promote it or retry nearby burst-count thresholds on the same frozen windows without forward rows or a materially sharper relation field.
next_evidence_needed: Forward replacement-value rows or a materially sharper free SEC relation field such as customer/supplier, supply-chain, or source-overlap context.

source_definition: SEC row must have pit_safe_flag true
same usable_trade_date and same event_family_bucket must have exactly two unique tickers
ticker must have exact signal-date OHLCV in the fixed snapshot
close must be above prior 50-day moving average
20-day average dollar volume must be at least USD 20 million
signal-day ticker-minus-SPY return must be no worse than -1 percentage point
signal-day close location must be at least 0.45
top-1 selected paper entry per signal date

prediction.confidence_reason: Read-only exp-20260530-006 showed small_burst_2 positive across all three windows, but an actual top-1 candidate-pool overlay may decay after OHLCV gating and overlap controls.

production_impact.promotion_requirement: A retained result would still require a shared default-off paper adapter and parity tests before any daily report or live/default behavior changes.

production_parity.parity_note: No production code path is changed. If accepted, promotion requires a shared event-family burst adapter that uses the same SEC PIT fields and signal-date OHLCV guards.

why_not_other_changes: Skipped LLM soft-ranking because candidate-level replay coverage remains sparse; skipped SEC structured financial-improvement fields because daily feature snapshots have zero populated same-accession financial-improvement rows in the fixed windows; skipped FINRA/state-surface/VCP scalar retunes per playbook freeze guidance. This tests one SEC event-graph candidate source.
